feeds.title: Photo Encaustic Blog
feeds.description: My purpose is to teach you about this amazing alternative photographic process called photo encaustic and give you the support, inspiration, and strategies to find your artistic vision using the medium. Clare O'Neill is a gifted instructor, she loves to share her passion for photograph and encaustic.

feeds.title: Natalie Salminen
feeds.description: Natalie Salminen teaches encaustic workshops both locally and internationally, exhibits and facilitates discussions on spirituality and what it means to live as an artist within the context of commitment. Encaustic has become for a valued medium as it allows for physicality, creative mixed media additions, use of poetic text and ultimately a powerful employment of color; each being vital components of her personal aesthetic and process.

feeds.title: Edge Of Grey Blog
feeds.description: Kim Kool is specialized in encaustic art, the ancient process of painting with beeswax, and offers a variety of creative classes and workshops for the community.

feeds.title: Elizabeth Hubler-Torrey Encaustic Fine Art Blog
feeds.description: Elizabeth Hubler-Torrey creates paintings and sculpture that reflect her inspiration from recent research in science, conservation, and climate change. Her naturally luminous creations have an internal glow from her use of beeswax and the technique of encaustic. She is self-taught in the medium of encaustic and is attracted to its versatility. Find more details about encaustic at Elizabeth Hubler-Torrey Encaustic Fine Art.

feeds.title: MARI RENWICK-ART Blog
feeds.description: Working with wax in an intimate, often combative, engagement, I am compelled by the challenge of manipulating this medium. Dragging, digging, and scraping are paramount responses in the process and facilitate my creating a surface of interest. Mari Renwick, is an encaustic painter, living and working in both Brooklyn and upstate NY. Her work is often influenced by the flora of the Catskills region, including the dried seed-pods and spent flowers remaining past the summer season.

feeds.title: EvAntArt » Encaustic
feeds.description: Get to know about encaustic art at EvAntArt. The subjects ranges from botanical illustration of garden and native flowers, to traditional landscape and energetic portrayals of waves releasing their energy as they impact rocks.
